races.name: Newark Advertiser Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Bondi
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won at 12f on Good going and has course-distance form, but 310 days off is a major concern and similar-going record on Fibresand reads 1 win from 8 — return to fitness is the primary question mark.

runners_data.name: Motazzen
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who won a 22f contest on Soft going and has headgear noted; veteran campaigner likely to press forward from a prominent position, but his best form is over extreme distances on different surfaces, and 82 days off must be factored in.

runners_data.name: Jindri
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam has had 3 winners from 11 in the last 14 days and Hector Crouch is an informed booking — however, this horse's genuine style is hold-up, and with the rear oversubscribed he will find himself racing more prominently than preferred, which tempers confidence despite strong course form showing 1W3P on this surface.

runners_data.name: Typical Woman
runners_data.note: Ian Williams runner whose best win came at 9f on Good, and she has failed to trouble the judge in six recent starts on Fibresand — her natural hold-up role is compromised in this field shape, sitting in midfield rather than the rear, which reduces the chance of delivering a telling late move.

runners_data.name: Gallant Lion
runners_data.note: Stablemate of Typical Woman, also trained by Ian Williams; won over 12f on Good ground and his best Southwell runs have come when able to close from off the pace, but similarly boxed into a midfield berth by the number of hold-up types, meaning his true closer's profile cannot be fully expressed.

runners_data.name: Domination
runners_data.note: Three-year-old on the upgrade — two wins from recent starts including a course win at 10f on Good — stepping up to 1m4f for the first time which is a legitimate query, but the form trajectory is upward and Sean Bowen's experience in getting hold-up horses into position is a real asset.

runners_data.name: Astrological
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's three-year-old boasts a 1W3P record on Fibresand from just four runs including a 12f win here, and his prominent style is perfectly suited to stalking Naples in a truly sustainable-pace scenario — one of the most course-and-distance-qualified runners in the field.

runners_data.name: Cliff Danger
runners_data.note: Pam Sly runner stepping up to 1m4f from a 10f best, but his four most recent form figures read 6-4-7-9 across surfaces and he has failed to place on Fibresand in two outings — difficult to make a case at this stage.

runners_data.name: Wonder
runners_data.note: Top-rated horse on OR 82 with an outstanding Fibresand record reading 2W9P from 14 runs at this course, all over 12f; James Fanshawe's hold-up specialist is 111 days off which is a fitness question, but if right he is the standout closer in the race and Taryn Langley's 5lb claim helps on the weights.

runners_data.name: Mehmas Champion
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old has been campaigned at 8f and is stepping well up in trip to 1m4f; Fibresand form shows just one run at this track with a poor finish, and the distance jump looks too ambitious to fancy with confidence.

runners_data.name: Yaa Min
runners_data.note: Hayley Burton runner who has 2 wins and 4 places from 11 starts on Fibresand, including recent placed efforts at 12f and 16f here — a genuine course specialist who will press from a prominent berth and is well-suited to a pace-controlled scenario behind Naples.

runners_data.name: Naples
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the race; won over 8f at Hea and drops back to a familiar front-running role with Dougie Costello, who is adept at judging pace — 53 days off is manageable, and the ability to dictate entirely unchallenged is a significant tactical advantage over 1m4f.

races.paceDynamic: Naples is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to apply pressure, Dougie Costello can dictate a controlled, measured gallop over this 1m4f Southwell Fibresand trip at Standard going. The field nominally contains several prominent and hold-up types — Astrological, Motazzen, and Yaa Min will push to sit handy behind Naples, while Jindri, Typical Woman, and Gallant Lion are genuine hold-up horses but are mapped to midfield because the rear is oversubscribed with closers, meaning they will be racing out of their most comfortable position. With Naples setting a sustainable tempo unchallenged, the race shape strongly favours horses who can track the pace from a prominent or close-stalking berth and produce a sustained gallop from the home turn, rather than those relying on a late sprint off a truly fast pace that simply will not materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Naples Dictates Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Naples is allowed to stride clear and set a controlled, uncontested pace throughout the 1m4f trip.
scenarios.body: Naples rolls along at a measured gallop giving himself maximum energy reserves, and Astrological or Yaa Min stalking just off the shoulder get a perfect tow into the straight before outstaying rivals. Prominent racers who travel efficiently behind a lone leader are the clear beneficiaries on this flat, Standard Fibresand track.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalkers Grind Naples Down
scenarios.trigger: If one or two prominent horses sit tight on Naples through the middle sector and apply sustained pressure from the 4f pole.
scenarios.body: Naples fades under close attention in the final two furlongs as the effort of leading from the front catches up, handing the race to a well-positioned tracker with a proven staying profile. Wonder, despite a hold-up tag, has strong Southwell form at this trip and could capitalise if produced with a well-timed move from midfield.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finish Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely in the straight, compressing the field and allowing a closing run from the rear.
scenarios.body: A breakdown in the sustainable tempo would create a rare opening for a horse with a strong finishing kick, but Jindri, Typical Woman, and Gallant Lion — the true closers — are mapped out of their natural position and may never secure the ideal pitch to deliver that run. Wonder has the strongest Southwell closing record here and is the most credible beneficiary if this scenario emerges.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Naples is taken on early by a prominent horse pushing forward unexpectedly, creating a fast early pace that leads to widespread fatigue.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected gallop burns off Naples and the pressing pack, leaving the race wide open for whoever is best placed at the top of the straight with energy intact. Domination, on a career-best trajectory and stepping up in trip, could prove the wildcard beneficiary of a chaotic shape.

watchPoints.text: Naples — monitor whether Dougie Costello is allowed a completely uncontested lead from the gates; if any horse jumps and challenges early, the whole pace dynamic shifts and the sustainable-tempo scenarios collapse.

Wonder — 111 days off the track for a hold-up horse who needs to be produced at exactly the right moment; if Taryn Langley is ring-rusty or the mare is short of peak fitness, her strong course record could be misleading today.

Gallant Lion and Typical Woman — both Ian Williams hold-up types who will be shuffled into midfield rather than their natural rear position; watch whether they end up boxed in behind a compressed pack in the straight with no clear run.

Astrological — has won at 12f at Southwell and should naturally find himself in the prime stalking position just off Naples; if he travels comfortably into the home turn, his course-and-distance form makes him a significant danger to the leader in the final furlong.

Domination — watch the betting market for this progressive three-year-old stepping up in trip; if punters support him strongly it may indicate trainer confidence that the 1m4f is within his compass, which would elevate his scenario relevance considerably.

races.name: Fraser Plus Designer Outlet East Midlands Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Love You More
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer who won over this C&D trip on Standard going and finished second here in her last run — the 34-day break is not a concern given that course form, and she has the best sim-going record in the field at 7 from 14 starts.|

runners_data.name: Implied Volatility
runners_data.note: Has run 10 times at this track over the mile on Standard going yet has never placed, suggesting a fundamental limitation rather than circumstance; 41 days off for Jennie Candlish, whose T14 reads 5/15, but the form string of 77-700 is discouraging.|

runners_data.name: The Spotlight Kid
runners_data.note: Consistent placer who has hit the frame five times in 15 sim-going starts for Dean Ivory, but as a true hold-up horse in a field overloaded with closers, she will likely be unable to find her natural rearward berth — Rob Hornby will need to adapt, which slightly undermines her chance despite good recent Southwell form.|

runners_data.name: Create
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on Good going and wears a hood; a genuine hold-up type who, because the rear of the field is overcrowded, will likely find herself operating further forward than ideal — her recent two wins do give her reason to respect, but the style mismatch is a factor.|

runners_data.name: Heretic
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has placed five times in 15 sim-going runs and shaped well when second last time out on Soft — wears tongue-strap and cheekpieces, and while undeniably effective from off the pace, the 66-day absence and the overcrowded hold-up section of this field are both worth noting.|

runners_data.name: Tardaff
runners_data.note: Has only one sim-going run in 8 starts and none of his last five outings on Standard has produced a place; Billy Loughnane takes a positive booking but the form figures of 54-005 offer little encouragement at this level.|

runners_data.name: Ribston Pippin
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner — she won over this C&D on Standard going and showed she can make all effectively; the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild note that her tendency is nominally prominent rather than a pure front-runner, but here she is the uncontested pace-setter and that is an asset, not a liability.|

runners_data.name: Barleybrown
runners_data.note: Has two career places over this C&D on Standard for Ruth Carr, so the course and trip are no concern; PJ McDonald is a strong booking and the p headgear confirms she likes to be ridden up with the pace — she is one of the few genuine prominent types in a field otherwise crammed with hold-up horses.|

runners_data.name: Mercurius Power
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with five places at this track over the mile on Standard, consistently prominent in his races thanks to tongue-strap and cheekpieces — Ray Dawson rides and the profile here is of a consistent, if non-winning, course specialist who should be allowed to track the leader throughout.|

runners_data.name: Splinterwood
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who has run four times on Standard AW, all at this track, and has never placed — a true hold-up horse for Michael Appleby who will be displaced further forward by the crowded rear of the field, and Daniel Muscutt takes over from a runner with a form string of 7-679.|

runners_data.name: Have You A Minute
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Standard and has placed four times in 13 sim-going starts for Tom Tate, but the 61-day layoff is notable and the step back to 8f from his recent runs over longer trips is a potential concern; Hector Crouch takes the ride on what is a genuine hold-up horse forced to race in midfield.|

runners_data.name: Muddy Marvellous
runners_data.note: Returning from 257 days off for Seb Spencer — by far the longest absence in the field — and carries the ⚠ fades in finish flag which is alarming for a hold-up horse; Dale Swift takes over and the form figures of 48/05- are deeply uninspiring.|

runners_data.name: Timebar
runners_data.note: Has placed twice in 10 sim-going starts and wears a tongue-strap; most of his best efforts have come over shorter trips of 5-6f, and this step up to a mile looks problematic based on his recent run profile, though Jack G Gilligan rides a horse that has shown some fight in placings.|

runners_data.name: Evelyn's Phoenix
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old has run six times recently without troubling the judge — the form string of 296906 is consistent in mediocrity — and wears tongue-strap and cheekpieces; Duran Fentiman rides and while the going is fine, the 8-9f trip on Standard suits on paper but the form gives no confidence.|

races.paceDynamic: Ribston Pippin is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner 1m Southwell handicap and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to pressure her into burning out early — she can set a controlled, measured tempo from the front and dictate entirely on her own terms. Behind her, Mercurius Power is likely to sit prominently alongside or just off her, while the bulk of the field — including The Spotlight Kid, Heretic, Create, Splinterwood, Have You A Minute, Timebar, Evelyn's Phoenix, Muddy Marvellous and others — are true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield simply because there is no room for them all to operate from the rear in this shape. The field holds significantly more genuine hold-up types than this race's pace map can naturally accommodate, with Ribston Pippin and Mercurius Power the only runners realistically likely to secure their natural forward positions. A single, uncontested front-runner dictating a steady, sustainable pace on Standard Southwell AW over a flat mile strongly favours the hold-up horse who can travel well in midfield and produce a sustained late run — though with so many true closers compressed into the middle of the pack and only one genuine pace-setter, the horse who tracks closest to the leader through the race will enjoy a significant tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ribston Pippin Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Ribston Pippin is allowed to bowl along in front entirely unopposed and sets a tempo that is comfortable enough to allow her to conserve energy for the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The uncontested lead on flat Southwell allows her to dictate every fraction of the race, and with Standard going suiting her profile and a recent win over this C&D, she is likely to prove tough to reel in from a winning position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Ribston Pippin is just quick enough to string the field out but leaves closers with enough to aim at in the straight.
scenarios.body: The compressed midfield of genuine hold-up horses — many racing out of their natural position — means one or two will find clear running and produce a strong sustained finish; the horse with the best turn of foot at this level will benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Mercurius Power travels smoothly just off Ribston Pippin's heels and picks up the pieces if the leader ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Mercurius Power has strong course and distance form with five placings at this track and handles Standard going well, making this a viable shape if Ribston Pippin overreaches or the pace quickens mid-race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Chaos From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely in the home straight and creates a bunched finish where runners at the very back can close the gap rapidly.
scenarios.body: With so many true hold-up horses unable to get their natural position, the most genuine rear-of-field types — Love You More, Implied Volatility, Tardaff — would benefit from a late scramble, though this shape is the least likely given the single front-runner setting a controlled rhythm.

watchPoints.text: Ribston Pippin's splits in the first two furlongs are critical — if she bowls along at a genuinely easy tempo with no challenger, she will be very hard to catch and the entire complexion of the race is decided in those early strides.

With seven or more true hold-up horses compressed into midfield, traffic in the straight is almost certain — watch for The Spotlight Kid and Heretic in particular, who need clear daylight late and may find their path blocked.

Mercurius Power must be monitored leaving the stalls — if he jumps cleanly and tucks in just behind Ribston Pippin, he is effectively racing from the ideal position; if he misses the break he loses his key tactical advantage entirely.

Muddy Marvellous's 257-day absence combined with the fades-in-finish flag makes her an early drifter to track in the market — significant money against her pre-race would confirm punter concern about her readiness and finishing resolve.

Barleybrown's p headgear and PJ McDonald's booking deserve monitoring — if she shows up in early market support, it suggests connections believe she can travel prominently enough to be dangerous if the pace is truly moderate.

races.name: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (Div I) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Assiri Heights
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 3yo showed fair form on debut at Goodwood over 6f but has been off 389 days, which is a major fitness concern; a true hold-up horse whose last run ended with a fade, and while the class is there, the return from such a lengthy absence on AW debut makes it hard to rely on.

runners_data.name: Blue Boy Junior
runners_data.note: David and Nicola Barron's 3yo has consecutive fourths on soft and good ground over 7f, showing consistency without winning; a natural rear-runner repositioned into midfield here because the field is so heavily loaded with hold-up types, meaning it races somewhat out of its comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Jetpack Jimmy
runners_data.note: Simon Whitaker's 3yo has one run to his name — a distant tenth over 7f at Southwell on Standard going — meaning the AW course and surface are familiar, but that form gives no confidence; holds up naturally yet will be pushed into a midfield slot in this shape, and repeated fading in finish flags are a concern.

runners_data.name: Mercantile
runners_data.note: Daniel and Claire Kubler's 3yo is completely unknown — no historical runs supplied and going preference is unverified; the Kubler yard has been in fair 14-day form (6/17) and Ebrahim Nader takes the ride, but with zero data this is a pure unknown quantity that could slot anywhere on the track.

runners_data.name: Palladas
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's 3yo won on debut over 8f at Southwell on Standard going — directly relevant form on this course and surface — and Billy Loughnane, one of the division's elite young jockeys, takes the ride after 200 days off; prominent by nature, a prominent position suits this race shape perfectly and the Godolphin operation rarely leave a horse like this underprepared.

runners_data.name: Cullinan Wolf
runners_data.note: Seb Spencer's 4yo has back-to-back poor efforts (7th, 8th) on Standard AW and Good ground over sprint trips; genuinely a hold-up type who will be squeezed into midfield in this field, meaning it races outside its natural style, and the uninspiring recent form offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Wats On Tiger
runners_data.note: Brian Rothwell's 4yo has a single run — ninth over 8f at Goodwood on Good — and Faye McManoman rides; a true closer whose last run ended with a fade over this exact trip, and competing on AW for the first time with modest credentials makes it hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Salvezza
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 3yo finished fifth on debut over 8f at Goodwood on Good ground 17 days ago, so arrives race-fit and tackles AW for the first time; Kieran Shoemark is a strong booking and this horse's natural hold-up style could suit if the pace is genuine enough — one to respect if fitness is there after a recent run.

runners_data.name: Star of The Desert
runners_data.note: Joey Ramsden's 3yo is the sole confirmed front-runner in the field and that role is confirmed, though the STYLE_FIT tag notes it may not always be entirely at home leading; placed on Standard AW over 8f (2nd at Southwell) gives direct course relevance, and Daniel Muscutt takes the ride — will control proceedings but finishing ability under pressure is the outstanding query.

runners_data.name: Wyvill
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's 3yo has consecutive sixths on Standard AW (10f) and Good ground (8f), both at trips longer than today's mile; David Probert is an astute jockey booking and this natural hold-up type may get a clear run from the rear, but the form is modest and dropping in trip slightly is an unknown.

runners_data.name: Regal Desire
runners_data.note: Non Runner — Brian Ellison's 3yo had place form on both Good and Standard AW over 8f, so was one of the more interesting prominent types; its withdrawal removes one of the few genuine pace-pressing threats to Star of The Desert and makes the front-runner's task even easier.

races.paceDynamic: Star of The Desert is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace pressure from another natural leader, will control the tempo from the front rail at a measured, sustainable gallop on Standard Fibresand. Palladas and Regal Desire (Non Runner) are the only other prominent-leaning types, meaning Star of The Desert faces minimal early challenge and can dictate the fractions throughout the mile. The bulk of this field — Assiri Heights, Blue Boy Junior, Jetpack Jimmy, Cullinan Wolf, Wyvill, Wats On Tiger and Salvezza — are natural hold-up horses, but the map cannot accommodate all of them at the rear, so several will be forced to race further forward than ideal; Jetpack Jimmy, Cullinan Wolf and Blue Boy Junior are most likely to actually secure midfield slots, while the truest closers (Assiri Heights, Wyvill, Salvezza) may get closest to their natural position. A controlled, uncontested gallop over a flat mile on Standard AW favours horses racing prominently who can quicken off an honest but unforced pace — the front-running and prominent profile is clearly best served here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Star Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Star of The Desert dictates an unchallenged, even gallop and the race is decided by a sustained stretch drive from the front.
scenarios.body: Star of The Desert bowls along in front setting fractions that suit herself, and Palladas, tracking in second, gets a dream prominent ride to pounce in the final furlong; the lack of genuine pressure means hold-up horses never get a true end-to-end test to close them down.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If Star of The Desert does set a genuinely strong early pace or the race quickens sharply, creating enough of a true end-to-end test for hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: Salvezza or Wyvill, able to settle in their natural position and produce a sustained late run, would benefit most from any uptick in tempo; Assiri Heights, despite a long absence, carries the class to land such a scenario if fitness holds.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is falsely slow early but several redistributed horses push up and cause a mid-race surge, turning it into a stamina-based grind.
scenarios.body: Blue Boy Junior and Cullinan Wolf, forced forward out of their natural hold-up roles, could be travelling well in mid-division and prove difficult to peg back if they find the pace tailor-made; this shape suits those with tactical versatility and fitness at the trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — No Shape Settles
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up types push forward en masse, creating an uneven pace with surges and stoppages that scrambles all positional plans.
scenarios.body: In a messy, stop-start affair, Mercantile (unknown style, unexposed) or Wyvill's quiet stamina could emerge as surprise beneficiaries; this scenario is low probability given the clear single pace-setter but cannot be ruled out entirely with 11 runners.

watchPoints.text: Star of The Desert (J: Daniel Muscutt) is the sole pace-setter — if she settles into a comfortable lead unchallenged, the race is effectively hers to lose and any horse trailing in her wake is racing into a headwind positionally.

Palladas has direct winning form at Southwell on Standard AW over 8f and Billy Loughnane will look to track Star of The Desert closely — watch how quickly he moves to second and whether he gets a clean passage into the straight.

With Regal Desire a non-runner, the early pace structure is even thinner than anticipated — monitor the early splits; an unusually slow gallop could compress the field and turn it into a sprint finish that scrambles all pace-map expectations.

Assiri Heights (T: Andrew Balding) returns after 389 days and is the highest-profile absentee in the field — watch the market moves and paddock presentation closely, as Balding's yard would not enter this horse without believing it is ready enough to show its true ability.

Salvezza (T: Ed Walker, J: Kieran Shoemark) is race-fit after 17 days and the combination of a top jockey and trainer who has been placing horses well (8/44 in 14 days) means it could outrun an unassuming debut fifth — watch for it to be produced late if the pace is honest.

races.name: LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes (Div II) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Al Jolson
runners_data.note: Unexposed three-year-old from the Simon & Ed Crisford yard who land big winners with lightly-raced types; unknown style but the top stable angle and Jack Mitchell booking suggest this is taken seriously, and a prominent pitch would suit the likely race shape.

runners_data.name: Electric Gambler
runners_data.note: Returned a 7th on his only start at Goodwood on turf; his natural instinct is to race from the rear, but with so many hold-up horses in this field he is likely to find himself busier early than his style demands, which tempers confidence in his chance here.

runners_data.name: Elite Approach
runners_data.note: Finished fourth on his only start over 6f at Southwell in Standard — the sim-going flag gives him a live each-way angle — though 109 days off the track and a 5lb claimer up is a concern; Taryn Langley rides for Joey Ramsden who operates at a low strike rate.

runners_data.name: Majestic Ruler
runners_data.note: Sole start produced a well-beaten sixth over 6f at Goodwood on good ground; the step up to a mile on Fibresand requires him to show much more than that debut effort, and Dylan Hogan's 1-from-4 T14 record is modest.

runners_data.name: Rua Mor
runners_data.note: Veteran of seven outings without a win, including two fifth-place efforts over 1m at Southwell in Standard going; his hold-up style on a flat track where the pace is controlled places him at a structural disadvantage, and 76 days off the track does not help.

runners_data.name: Prosperity
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field; won on his sole start over 1m at Goodwood and arrives 20 days later for K.R. Burke who is bang in form at 4-from-32 over 14 days; his ability to control fractions makes him the race's pivotal horse even if the STYLE_FIT tag acknowledges he is mapped as prominent.

runners_data.name: Peaceful Spirit
runners_data.note: Has not run in 499 days — by far the longest absence in the field — and carries that layoff into a competitive novice stakes; two Southwell runs suggest some familiarity with the track (1W0P in sim-going), but a hold-up style and near-two-year-break make this a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Savile Row
runners_data.note: The OR-80 outsider of the field, yet brings multiple runs of experience and a prominent racing style that suits the projected pace scenario; best effort was a runner-up over 6f on soft, so the step up to a mile on Fibresand is untested, but Anthony Brittain occasionally targets these spots.

runners_data.name: Sotto Il Sasso
runners_data.note: Debutant for Brian Meehan who is a capable handler of unexposed three-year-olds; Joe Leavy takes the ride with no form to assess style or going preference, making him a pure wildcard whose chance hinges entirely on ability concealed on the gallops.

runners_data.name: Ze Gucci Poochie
runners_data.note: Finished a distant tenth on his only start over 7f at Southwell in Standard going and carries a "fades in finish" flag — both factors point against him on a flat, fair track where hold-up horses need to travel powerfully; 24 days between runs is straightforward.

runners_data.name: My Prerogative
runners_data.note: Experienced two outings — fifth at Goodwood and eighth at Southwell — suggesting limited improvement in this grade; his natural hold-up style means he is unlikely to secure the prominent position he needs to be competitive in this shape, and the STYLE_FIT discount applies on both counts.

races.paceDynamic: Prosperity is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner field and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, Pierre-Louis Jamin should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on the Southwell AW mile. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching — one leader at a Standard-going Fibresand mile sets up a race that could compress late, rewarding those who track the pace rather than those buried deep. The bulk of the field — Rua Mor, Peaceful Spirit, Ze Gucci Poochie, My Prerogative and Electric Gambler — are genuine hold-up horses, meaning there is a significant cluster of horses likely to be racing at the back with limited room to land a telling blow unless the pace unravels. The race shape therefore favours prominent-to-mid division runners who can slot in behind Prosperity and launch their challenge from a position of awareness; those racing truly off the pace need the front-runner to crater, which is less likely when the pace is uncontested. Note that the field contains more hold-up types than can realistically be accommodated at the rear of the field, and the runners most likely to actually secure a forward position — aside from Prosperity — are Al Jolson and Elite Approach, whose style is unclassified but who may travel more prominently than their rivals.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prosperity Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Prosperity is allowed to dictate an uncontested, measured gallop and no rival has the early pace to pressurise from the outside.
scenarios.body: Jamin sets fractions to suit on a flat track, and the leader simply stays fresh enough to repel challengers in the final furlong; any horse tracking second or third and travelling comfortably becomes the main danger.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracking Prosperity in second or third position conserves energy through the middle of the race and produces a sustained run from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: The controlled early gallop leaves Prosperity exposed to a rival who has switched off behind and hits full stride just as the leader begins to feel the mile; this suits a horse with an unraced or lightly-raced profile that may be fitter than their form reads.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If Prosperity goes too fast for the conditions or the field crowds the early pace and a faster-than-expected gallop sets up a strong late run.
scenarios.body: Hold-up horses tracking midfield could pick up the pieces if the front-runner burns out, though this is a less likely shape given Prosperity is uncontested and unlikely to over-cook the fractions; Rua Mor and Peaceful Spirit would be the primary beneficiaries if this shape materialised.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Upset, Rank Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the race is muddling and unpredictable, producing a chaotic finish where unexposed lightly-raced runners outclass the field on raw ability.
scenarios.body: Savile Row brings course form and a prominent style that could see it travel well from a manageable draw, while Ze Gucci Poochie's finishing concerns make a winning effort unlikely unless the race is run at a crawl.

watchPoints.text: Prosperity (Jamin/Burke) has a clear run to the lead with zero pace rivals — if he settles smoothly in the early stages, watch whether any rival has the tactical speed to close the gap entering the final two furlongs.

Peaceful Spirit has not run in 499 days and is a hold-up type on a track where the pace is controlled — monitor in the betting for any unexpected support that might signal stable confidence, but structurally she is compromised.

Electric Gambler and My Prerogative are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map; watch at the start to see whether they are able to slot further back than their mapped positions — if they are stuck wide and prominent, their race plans are immediately disrupted.

Al Jolson and Sotto Il Sasso are both debutants for high-profile yards (Crisford, Meehan) with no public form — watch the early market moves close to post time, as stable confidence in lightly-raced types from these operations often surfaces in the ring.

Elite Approach is the only runner with a Southwell sim-going run in the field (4th/6f/Standard) — watch whether Taryn Langley attempts to track Prosperity early, as any horse able to hold that prominent position behind the pace-setter is well-placed given the projected race shape.

races.name: Coopers Marquees Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Tina's Indian
runners_data.note: Blinkered prominent racer who landed a 7f Hea win last time but has three consecutive poor efforts at Goodwood in between; Billy Loughnane rides for a trainer with a solid 2/7 14-day record and the return to Fibresand (won 6f here previously) suits, though 65 days off and a high OR of 92 make this a stiff ask from a prominent pitch in a busy early-pace race.

runners_data.name: Willem Twee
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up performer with a remarkable Southwell record — 1 win and 5 places from 15 Standard starts — who has hit the board back-to-back here over 7f; Rob Hornby continues the partnership and viscous Fibresand suits his grinding style, though a 0/4 trainer run in 14 days is a mild flag on the day.

runners_data.name: Skipper
runners_data.note: Returned from 83 days off carrying blinkers, and his two Southwell wins (1W, 2P from 8 visits) suggest he handles the track well; James Doyle is an upgrade, and the drop back to 7f from a string of 8f runs looks ideal, though today's busy prominent berth means he may get squeezed for position early.

runners_data.name: Dixieland Blues
runners_data.note: The sole natural front-runner and therefore the key pace-setter for the whole race; Simon & Ed Crisford have an excellent 14-day record (8/24) and he has won twice at Southwell over 7f and 8f on Standard, but the 326-day absence is the dominant risk factor and his ability to sustain his natural lead role after such a gap is genuinely uncertain.

runners_data.name: Aurora Majesty
runners_data.note: Won twice and placed twice in 11 starts for Archie Watson (0/23 in 14 days — a flag), but his natural instinct to race prominently means he is likely to find himself further back than ideal in this field of prominent types; Pierre-Louis Jamin may attempt to secure a front-rank position but faces a traffic puzzle, and a 15-day turnaround adds a fitness query.

runners_data.name: Valvano
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's 7/34 14-day form is strong, and Hector Crouch rides the highest-rated runner in the field at OR 95; however, Valvano's recent form is built around 8-12f on soft/heavy and he has only one Southwell run (unplaced on Standard), making this trip and surface a concern after 141 days off.

runners_data.name: Legal Reform
runners_data.note: Exceptional Southwell specialist with 3 wins and 8 places from 15 starts on Standard at this track, and David Probert has the course-form knowledge to position him perfectly; returned from 156 days off last time to win at 7f here, making that a confirmed prep, and the prominent style slots neatly into the pace shape — the outstanding statistical profile for this track demands respect.

runners_data.name: Midnight Thunder
runners_data.note: Saeed bin Suroor's yard won with him twice on good ground but this is his first run in 569 days and first start on Fibresand; Kieran O'Neill takes the ride and the ability is clearly there (OR 94, wins at 6f), but the extreme layoff and complete absence of all-weather form introduce substantial risk in what is an open enough handicap.

runners_data.name: Great Dream
runners_data.note: Won last time at 8f on soft, beating soft-ground rivals, and Dale Swift for Seb Spencer (1/6 in 14 days) is a workmanlike combination; the drop to 7f on Fibresand is a new test and his Southwell record is thin (1W, 2P from 10 starts on similar ground), but he arrives in decent current form with only 60 days between runs.

runners_data.name: Shiplake
runners_data.note: Won twice on Standard at Southwell in his last two starts here, so the track clearly suits, and Daniel Muscutt is a strong course partner; his true style is front-running/prominent and he will want to be near the action, but with six prominent types ahead of him in the pecking order he may find himself further back than ideal, making his usual Southwell aggression harder to replicate.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Ocean
runners_data.note: Young three-year-old who won at Southwell over 7f on Standard (1W, 1P from 5 visits), making him one of the more course-relevant runners; Marco Ghiani for Marco Botti (4/18 in 14 days) is a live combination and an OR of 93 gives him plenty of weight concessions against older rivals, though only 50 days between runs and a step up in handicap grade after Goodwin defeats are the checks.

runners_data.name: Utmost Good Faith
runners_data.note: Won at 7f on good at Goodwood and carries strong Goodwood form, but Fibresand on Standard is an entirely different surface proposition — only 3 unplaced runs from 11 tries at similar-going venues suggests the track may not suit; Stuart Williams (3/31 in 14 days) keeps the faith, Ray Dawson rides, and a tongue-tie/cheekpieces combination adds a gear change.

runners_data.name: Divine Libra
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who placed twice on Standard-style going (including a 2nd at Southwell), but recent form shows a string of midfield finishes (11th, 5th, 8th, 8th) and the OR of 87 suggests he is at a career plateau; Charles Hills (5/17 in 14 days) has the operation ticking and Jason Watson rides well here, but only 1 place from 15 tries on similar going is a sobering number.

runners_data.name: Kisskodi
runners_data.note: Owns two wins and two places at 7f, including wins on soft and Standard, and George Wood for Harry Eustace (1/8 in 14 days) is a competitive pairing; by nature a front-runner who has won prominently, he will find this field overcrowded ahead of him and his energy may be spent covering ground rather than controlling the race as he has done at his best.

races.paceDynamic: Dixieland Blues is the sole confirmed front-runner and, returning from 326 days off for the Crisford yard, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on Standard Fibresand with no natural challenger to his lead — this creates a controlled, single-file pace rather than a true hot-pace scenario. Six of the fourteen runners carry prominent intentions, but the track simply cannot accommodate them all: Tina's Indian, Skipper, Valvano, Legal Reform, Great Dream, and Sovereign Ocean will all press for the prominent berths immediately behind Dixieland Blues, generating significant traffic friction between the 2f and 3f-out markers as the field concertinas on the turn. Aurora Majesty, Shiplake, and Kisskodi are genuine prominent racers by inclination but have been displaced into mapped midfield positions because the field is over-subscribed for that position — those three are most likely to find themselves shuffled back against their wishes. The resulting shape — a lone leader, a congested chasing pack, and a wide, flat Southwell track — tilts the race toward horses with natural prominent ability who can travel smoothly within the first three or four, preserving energy through the bunching, rather than pure hold-up types who will have ground to make up off a tempo that is unlikely to be truly punishing.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dixieland Blues Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Dixieland Blues bowls along uncontested and the prominent pack behind him cannot sustain their challenge, allowing the leader to hold on or for the best-travelling prominent horse to pounce close home.
scenarios.body: Dixieland Blues controls fractions off a modest gallop, and the horse who travels most fluently just off the pace — not burning petrol in the early scrimmage — swoops in the final furlong; Legal Reform's exceptional Southwell record (3 wins, 8 places from 11 starts here) and Sovereign Ocean's course-winning form make them the likeliest beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Opens Late
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent racers creates enough sustained pressure through the middle of the race that the pace fractionally quickens and Dixieland Blues is reeled in, opening the door for hold-up horses to finish through.
scenarios.body: The congestion between 3f and 2f out causes shuffling and minor checks that benefit those with a clear run from behind; Willem Twee's strong Southwell form (1 win, 5 places in 15 starts on Standard, including back-to-back 3rds here) and Utmost Good Faith, who won at 7f on good ground and can produce a late burst, are best placed to pick up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Congestion Chaos Favours Wide Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent traffic jam produces significant interference on the final turn, forcing multiple horses to check or switch, gifting an advantage to those wide and unobstructed.
scenarios.body: Hold-up horses tracking the outside avoid the worst of the scrimmage and arrive with momentum intact in the final furlong; Divine Libra has placed twice on similar going at Southwell-style tracks and Midnight Thunder — fit-again for Saeed bin Suroor after 569 days — may use class to travel wide and power through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfield Sweeps
scenarios.trigger: If Dixieland Blues' long absence (326 days) takes its toll and he fades sharply inside the final 2f, collapsing the pace and triggering a wall-to-wall sprint finish.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a dash for the line from 2f out and horses with fresh legs and tactical speed who have not spent energy pressing the leader gain most; Kisskodi and Aurora Majesty — both natural front-runners squeezed back but retaining tactical speed — can produce a late burst if they avoid the bunching.

watchPoints.text: Dixieland Blues (Jack Mitchell) is the sole pace-setter and if his 326-day absence tells in the final furlong, the entire race shape collapses — monitor him in the paddock and the first two furlongs for any sign of jumping awkwardly or over-racing.

Traffic congestion between the 3f and 2f markers is the single biggest race-shape risk — with Tina's Indian, Skipper, Valvano, Legal Reform, Great Dream, and Sovereign Ocean all pressing for the same three or four positions, a flash-point shuffle or check on the home turn could eliminate several prominent-side contenders in a single move.

Aurora Majesty, Shiplake, and Kisskodi are all natural prominent racers who will attempt to find a forward position despite being mapped to midfield — watch the first furlong to see whether any of them force their way up; if one succeeds, Dixieland Blues may face unexpected pressure and the sustainable-pace scenario unravels.

Legal Reform is 156 days between his last win and today's run, and while that last win was confirmed at Southwell, a lengthy absence in a fast early-pace environment with traffic danger means his prominent pitch could be physically costly if he gets boxed in around the 3f pole.

Midnight Thunder (Kieran O'Neill, Saeed bin Suroor) is the wildcard of the field — 569 days off and no Fibresand form, but an OR of 94 and two previous wins suggest raw talent; watch whether the yard has him visibly sharp at the start, as a well-prepared return could see him storm through late on a day when prominent runners are busy scrapping.

races.name: Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (Div I) (GBB Race)
Grace & Dotty Maiden Stakes (Div II) (GBB Race)
Gb Civil Engineering Apprentice Handicap Stakes (Apprentice Training Race - Part Of The Racing Excellence Series)

runners_data.name: Southern Warrior
runners_data.note: Won over C&D on his last visit to Southwell on standard going, progressive 3yo with hold-up style; carried to midfield here by redistribution, so will need things to open up late, but C&D form is the key positive angle.

runners_data.name: Orange Emperor
runners_data.note: Consistent 3yo who showed speed to finish third over 6f on good, but his five-run history contains no wins and a concern over soft ground suggests standard suits; a natural hold-up type who needs a strong pace to make ground.

runners_data.name: Federal Envoy
runners_data.note: Trainer Charlie Clover sends this five-year-old in fresh form (12 days since last run) and he has course form over 7f; genuinely a hold-up horse pushed forward on the pace map, so his chance depends on a stronger-than-expected pace developing — modest style-fit score of 0.92 tempers optimism.

runners_data.name: On Key
runners_data.note: Legitimate prominent racer with an excellent record at Southwell, including a win and six places over course and distance on standard; Scott Dixon has a live yard (2/11 last 14 days) and Charlie Tucker is apprentice claim — this is the standout profile for the dominant race shape.

runners_data.name: Ahead Of Fashion
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo (63 days off) who showed ability when second over 7f at Southwell on standard, but the step back to 6f on a track where she has limited experience is a query; her hold-up nature means she sits behind others on the map, and the style-fit flag (0.92) reflects the challenge of getting a clean run here.

runners_data.name: Blackjack
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran who handles standard Southwell well (14/15 runs in similar conditions) and has placed here before, but a hold-up style crammed into a crowded midfield-rear alongside six similar types means clear passage is a genuine concern; style-fit score 0.93.

runners_data.name: Torfrida
runners_data.note: Has raced predominantly at 5f and all five recent runs have been over sprint trips shorter than today's 6f — the step up in distance is a meaningful concern; a natural hold-up type shuffled to midfield on the map, and with only one run on standard Southwell going, this is the thinnest course-form profile in the race.

runners_data.name: Big Apple Jack
runners_data.note: Showed encouragement when second at 6f on good going but has one run on standard Southwell (finishing eighth) and his trainer Easterby stable runs at just 3/30 in the past 14 days; a genuine hold-up horse whose redistribution to midfield compounds the challenge of finding daylight.

runners_data.name: Great Success
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted 3yo with a string of mid-pack finishes on good going but no experience of standard Southwell — all five recent runs are on good ground; hold-up style and zero course form in these conditions make this one of the most speculative profiles in the field.

runners_data.name: Starsong
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner, seven-year-old veteran of Michael Appleby's yard, who faces no pace pressure and can set a controlled gallop throughout; he has placed at 6f on good but winning form eludes him — his value is as the pace-setter who may last home rather than a certain winner.

runners_data.name: Massimo Blue
runners_data.note: Consistent course specialist with two wins and five places from 13 starts on standard Southwell at 6f — the standout C&D record in the race; a hold-up type by style but the course knowledge and form in conditions is hard to dismiss, and top weight of 140lbs is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Tough Enough
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose best recent form is a second at 6f on standard (Southwell), but six-run form string includes a 12th and a 10th suggesting inconsistency; the 140lb top weight shared with Massimo Blue is a burden, and Antony Brittain's yard is running at just 1/6 over the past 14 days.

runners_data.name: Lesley's Boy
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey yard in good form (4/29 last 14 days) and this four-year-old has placed on standard Southwell at 6f, but 62 days off the track is a noteworthy absence; a true hold-up horse pushed onto the pace map by redistribution, so the style-fit concern (0.91) is real.

runners_data.name: Toptime
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a win at 5f on soft and consistent placed form, but all five recent runs are at 5f — the step to 6f is an untested distance on standard Southwell; a genuine prominent-style runner who should be close to the pace, and Roy Bowring's yard is live (2/5 last 14 days).

races.paceDynamic: Starsong is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner 6f handicap and, crucially, faces no genuine pace pressure — she can dictate her own rhythm from the gates and set a sustainable, controlled tempo rather than a punishing gallop. On Key and Toptime are the likeliest horses to push up into prominent positions and track Starsong at close quarters, with Massimo Blue and Tough Enough also capable of sitting handy from their natural styles. This field contains more hold-up and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Federal Envoy, Lesley's Boy, Ahead Of Fashion, Blackjack, Big Apple Jack, Torfrida and Great Success are all genuine hold-up runners who have been redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning the rear ranks will be crowded and those horses will be racing in tighter quarters than they'd like. With one genuine pace-setter setting a measured gallop and a congested field behind, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently close to the controlled fractions and produce their effort early, rather than closers who must find gaps from the back in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Starsong Controls, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Starsong is allowed to stride clear and set a sustainable pace, prominent trackers deliver their challenge over the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Starsong dictates in front without being headed or pressured, keeping fractions honest enough to reward those who have tracked her throughout; On Key and Toptime, as genuine prominent types with solid course and distance form, are ideally placed to pounce close home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Two Pulled Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace allows Starsong and whichever prominent horse sits second to steadily lengthen stride and draw clear without a genuine challenge from behind.
scenarios.body: With no pace pressure to slow Starsong down, the lead pair could simply steal the race by sustaining their gallop through the final two furlongs while the hold-up pack gets stuck in traffic; horses like On Key and Massimo Blue, who have the natural pace to sit close, benefit most from this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is quicker than expected and the front runners tire noticeably inside the final furlong, allowing midfield types to pick them off.
scenarios.body: Federal Envoy and Southern Warrior, though racing at least partially out of their most natural position, carry enough ability to close if the lead pair weaken sharply; this scenario is discounted because several redistributed hold-up types face a congested run and are unlikely to find clear passage in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Backmarkers Struck Off
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly dawdling and the entire field fans wide turning for home, creating a sprint finish that disadvantages true hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A genuine sprint finish theoretically opens the door for any horse with residual toe, but the redistributed hold-up horses — Blackjack, Great Success, Torfrida, Big Apple Jack — have style-fit concerns and poor course form that makes them unlikely beneficiaries even if gaps appear; Massimo Blue's consistent course form gives him the best claims here if the scenario materialises.

watchPoints.text: On Key is a genuine prominent racer with multiple C&D wins and places on standard Southwell — watch for Charlie Tucker to position him close to Starsong from the off, as this is exactly the profile the race shape suits.

Massimo Blue's C&D record (2 wins, 5 places from 13 runs on standard Southwell at 6f) is the strongest course form in the race — despite top weight and a hold-up tag, watch for Kyle McHugh to push forward earlier than expected given the field shape.

The seven hold-up runners crammed into the midfield-rear create a significant traffic problem in the straight — watch for Federal Envoy, Lesley's Boy and Blackjack to get blocked if the field bunches, as their true style leaves them needing gaps that may not materialise.

Torfrida's trip concern is worth monitoring in-running — all five recent starts have been over 5f, and if she fades sharply inside the final furlong having been asked to sustain a longer effort, it confirms the distance as a genuine issue rather than a one-off.

Starsong's early sectionals deserve close attention — if she is allowed to stride clear unchallenged through the first two furlongs, the race could effectively be set up as a two-horse contest between her and whichever prominent tracker sits closest, rather than a genuine sprint finish for the field.
